newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik peace talks postponed - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Tajik peace talks postponed - Tass.

text.p: Peace talks between the Tajik president and the leader of the former Soviet republic's Islamic opposition, due to start in Moscow on Thursday morning, have been postponed, Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said.

The agency quoted a spokesman for Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who had been planning to take part in the talks. Security personnel at the venue for the meeting told a Reuters photographer the event had been cancelled.

Chernomyrdin's office said the prime minister had already left for another engagement. But an official said he had no information about any postponment of the discussions, which were due to deal with a peace plan for the former Soviet republic.

A series of Tajik ceasefire deals have collapsed, some of them as soon as they were signed. Local officials have reported fighting between government troops and the Islamist opposition in the Garm region, in clear violation of the latest pact.

The Moscow talks were to be attended by Chernomyrdin and by Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri. Tass, in a report from the Iranian capital Tehran, said Nuri had left there for Moscow on Thursday morning.

Richard Morczynski, political officer with the U.N. observers, said in Dushanbe he still expected the meeting to take place. "Mr Nuri is expected to come to Moscow. If he arrives early this afternoon, the talks will take place today (Thursday). If Mr Nuri arrives tomorrow, they will start then."
